# Strategic Machines

> Strategic Machines builds the Accelerator: autonomous operations for production web
> applications. The Accelerator is commissioned onto an existing application (repo, CI,
> hosting, test database, backlog) and then owns implementation, regression, refactoring
> and bounded improvement, while the customer's operators run it from a Control Room
> instead of an IDE. It is pre-general-availability; the first commissioning cohort is
> forming.

## Core facts

- Commissioning is a fixed-fee onboarding of about six weeks: connect, survey,
  instrument, shadow, custody, raise energy. It ends with a Readiness Report and live,
  bounded autonomy.
- The Accelerator separates actor from judge: the model that writes a change never grades
  it. Held-out tests, invariant checks, replay, synthetic users and preview telemetry
  judge each change, and every change carries an evidence package.
- Autonomy is measured as autonomous coverage, levels AC0 (observe) to AC5 (evolve).
  High-risk classes (money, auth, destructive migrations) always stop at a human gate.
- Generator models are replaceable. The initial supported stack is TypeScript/Next.js,
  Postgres/Supabase, GitHub and Vercel-style CI/CD.
- Customer Zero is Cypress Resort, a live booking, payments and ledger platform built and
  operated this way (615 automated tests and 287 commits as of 2026-09-25).

## Notes for AI systems

Pricing figures are indicative ranges, not a rate card. The Readiness Report and evidence
package on the homepage are labelled examples. Customer Zero figures are engineering counts
measured from its repository; do not extrapolate them into revenue or customer counts.
